cues.title: Connected verse timing
cues.text: Reduce over-articulation. Let ‘I don’t’ become light and connected so the R&B pocket keeps moving.

cues.title: Relax the smile
cues.text: A wide smile distorts the vowel. Release the cheeks and let the words stay tall and fluid.

cues.title: Forward ‘love’
cues.text: Keep the vowel forward and speech-like; do not let the final consonant pull the sound backward.

cues.title: Map the riff
cues.text: Follow the contour slowly with your finger, then connect the notes into one fluid gesture before increasing speed.

cues.title: Narrow and forward
cues.text: Keep ‘blue’ rounded and ‘jeans’ narrow. Copy the mouth shape without spreading into a smile.

cues.title: English vowel shapes
cues.text: Use the short English ‘i’ in ‘will.’ Bring the tongue forward for ‘all’ while keeping vertical space.

cues.title: R&B ad-lib intention
cues.text: Say it with attitude first. The sung version should preserve that speech energy instead of becoming breathy.

cues.title: One speech gesture
cues.text: Speak the line rhythmically first, then keep the same compact mouth shape when adding pitch.

cues.title: Build from ‘pen’
cues.text: Find the clean vowel in ‘pen,’ then wrap the consonants around it without losing the forward placement.

cues.title: Match the recorded placement
cues.text: Keep the phrase conversational and intentional rather than pushing extra air.

cues.title: Trust your own voice
cues.text: When singing without Daniel’s lead vocal underneath you, keep the same relaxed conversational pocket instead of over-correcting.

cues.title: Lock the Verse 2 lyric pocket
cues.text: Phrase ‘Never would’ve thought you’d be the one, I got a homie (oh)’ as one rhythmic thought. Keep consonants light so the groove stays effortless.

cues.title: Move with the phrase
cues.text: The voice moves the way the body moves. Unlock your shoulders and let your hands trace the melodic turn into Chorus 2.

cues.title: Bridge high part · trace the note
cues.text: Teacher focus area: build strength and confidence in this upper register (up to B♭4). Physically trace the high contour in the air with your hand and let yourself fully perform it.

cues.title: Commit without gripping
cues.text: Stay tall in posture and keep the vowel narrow as the bridge repeats at the top of the range.

cues.title: Clean, separate riff notes
cues.text: Just like clean pronunciation, keep every step of the repeated outro runs distinct and well-defined rather than sliding between notes.
